item.title: China urges the Philippines to stop playing up South China Sea issue in multilateral fora
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-29
UNITED NATIONS, Sept. 29 (Xinhua) -- A Chinese envoy said Monday that the Philippines should stop playing up the South China Sea issue in multilateral fora and should, instead, return to the bilateral track. In exercising the right of reply at the General Debate of the 81st session of the UN General Assembly, Sun Lei, China's deputy permanent representative to the United Nations, said that with regard to the Philippine statement delivered at the debate on Saturday, China has consistently maintained that the United Nations is not the appropriate forum to discuss the South China Sea issue. However, he said, China finds it necessary to issue a solemn response to the relevant erroneous claims by the Philippines. China's position on the so-called "South China Sea arbitration" has been consistent and clear, Sun said. The Philippines' unilateral initiation of arbitration violates fundamental principles of international law, including state consent and pacta sunt servanda, and contravenes the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, he added. The "arbitral tribunal" exceeded its authority and abused its jurisdiction. The so-called "award" it rendered is illegal, null and void. China neither accepts nor recognizes the "award," and opposes and will never accept any claim or action arising from it, said Sun. This is both to safeguard China's own territorial and maritime rights and interests and to uphold the international maritime rule of law and a fair and equitable international maritime order, he said. The Philippine attempt to play up the 10th anniversary of the so-called "award" is utterly meaningless. The fact is that the "award" has not only failed to resolve the maritime issues between China and the Philippines, but has also exacerbated regional tensions, becoming a stumbling block to China-Philippines relations and to peace and stability in the South China Sea, he said. China does not accept any imposed solution with respect to territorial issues and maritime delimitation disputes, and remains committed to resolving the disputes through negotiation and consultation with countries directly concerned. China will continue to work with members of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations to jointly safeguard peace and stability in the South China Sea, he said. China urges the Philippines to stop playing up the issue in multilateral fora, return as soon as possible to the right track of bilateral consultations, work with China to manage South China Sea disputes, and work together to safeguard peace and stability in the South China Sea, said Sun. ■

item.title: China expects bumper grain harvest for 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-29
BEIJING, Sept. 29 (Xinhua) -- China is expected to secure a bumper grain harvest this year, the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs said Tuesday. This year, summer grain output exceeded 150 million tonnes for the first time, and early rice output remained above 28 million tonnes for the sixth consecutive year, the ministry said at a press conference. Autumn crops, the mainstay of China's annual grain production, are now being harvested, with the planted area expanded and that of high-yielding crops, particularly corn, increasing notably, according to Zhang Zhu, minister of agriculture and rural affairs. "Against the backdrop of increased volatility in global grain markets, China has a solid foundation and ample confidence to ensure stable grain production and supply," said Zhang. ■

item.title: Xi-Trump summit raises expectations for greater global stability: scholar
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-29
SINGAPORE, Sept. 29 (Xinhua) -- The recent summit between Chinese President Xi Jinping and U.S. President Donald Trump has added new substance to the constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability, raising expectations for greater stability around the world, a public policy scholar has said. By agreeing to build "a constructive relationship of strategic stability based on respect, fairness and reciprocity," the two presidents have provided a paradigm for countries to resolve differences fairly, said Gu Qingyang, an associate professor at the Lee Kuan Yew School of Public Policy at the National University of Singapore, in an interview with Xinhua. The new vision shows that China and the United States are willing to resolve differences on the basis of respecting each other's development paths and core interests, while allowing reasonable room for each other's development and taking into account the common interests of both countries and the wider world, he said. It also reflects a commitment to treating each other as equal partners, pursuing mutual benefit and balancing rights and obligations, Gu said. "It offers new ideas for a complex international environment and gives a troubled world a reassuring anchor of stability," Gu said, noting that countries, regardless of size or strength, should resolve differences and manage disputes through consultation on an equal footing rather than through zero-sum competition. Gu said Xi's remarks that building a constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability is neither an expedient measure nor something that can be achieved overnight reflects a key feature of China's approach to relations with the United States: a long-term perspective. It requires action of all sectors, across all fields and at all levels in the two countries while looking to lasting engagement across generations, he said, citing Xi's invitation for 100,000 young Americans to visit China for exchanges and study programs over the next five years. This is, in effect, about engaging younger generations and building lasting ties between the people of the two countries, Gu said. "China and the United States, as two major countries, need to engage across all fronts to understand each other's concerns and interests, and build a relationship in which their interests are mutually reinforcing," he said. ASEAN countries welcome candid dialogue between China and the United States and hope it will help make the regional and global environment more stable and predictable, he said. Gu said ASEAN countries see the next decade as critical for development, while at the same time, they have felt the impact of global uncertainty, including disruptions to industrial and supply chains in recent years caused by unilateral tariffs and practices of decoupling and supply chain severance. Looking ahead, Gu said the interests of China and the United States, as well as those of the wider world, require the two countries to avoid confrontation. A constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability will help create a relatively stable environment for China, the United States and the wider world over the medium and long term, he said. ■

item.title: Xi urges Sichuan University to leverage strengths in serving national strategies
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-29
BEIJING, Sept. 29 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping has urged Sichuan University to leverage its interdisciplinary strengths and play a pioneering and exemplary role in serving national strategies, as he extended congratulations on the 130th founding anniversary of the university. Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks in a reply letter to the university's teachers and students. In the letter, Xi congratulated the university's faculty members, students and alumni on the anniversary. He noted that serving the country with dedication, taking root in western China, and fostering talent through education are fine traditions of Sichuan University. Xi expressed the hope that the university will carry forward its revolutionary legacy, leverage its strengths of interdisciplinary integration across humanities, sciences, engineering and medicine, and contribute to building China into a leading country in education, science and technology, and talent development. The history of Sichuan University dates back to the Sichuan Chinese and Western School founded in 1896, the earliest institution of higher learning in southwest China. ■

item.title: China sweeps sprint relays as two Games records fall
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-28
NAGOYA, Japan, Sept. 28 (Xinhua) -- China continued its strong athletics campaign at the 2026 Asian Games on Monday, winning four gold medals, including both 4x100m relay titles, while the UAE's Mariam Kareem and Japan's Kazuto Iizawa set Asian Games records. Kareem, 18, won the women's 400m hurdles in 54.31 seconds, lowering the previous Games record of 54.45 set by Bahrain's Oluwakemi Adekoya at Hangzhou in 2023. Kazakhstan's Adelina Zems and India's Vithya Ramraj both set personal bests to take silver and bronze, respectively, while China's Kong Yingying finished fourth in 55.78. Qatar's Bassem Hemeida won the men's 400m hurdles in 47.82, followed by Japan's Taiju Goto and Chinese Taipei's Lin Chung-wei. Iizawa also set an Asian Games record, clocking 3:36.35 to win the men's 1,500m. India's Gulveer Singh took silver and Japan's Nagiya Mori bronze, while China's Liu Dezhu finished fourth. Iizawa became the first Japanese man in 40 years to win the Asian Games 1,500m title. "What was asked of me was a gold medal, and I am glad I delivered it," Iizawa said. "The clock on the Japanese men's 1,500m had been stopped for a very long time, and I think I have started it moving again, little by little. I do not want to stop at this. I want to go higher." In the women's discus, China's Feng Bin defended her title with a final-round throw of 63.83 meters. Compatriot Jiang Zhichao took silver with a season-best 62.25m, while Thailand's Subenrat Insaeng also set a season best with 61.43m for bronze. Despite winning gold, the 32-year-old Feng said she had mixed feelings about her performance. "I reached my goal in ranking, but I missed my target mark by a little," said Feng, who had hoped to throw 65 or 66 meters. Injuries had prevented Feng from training consistently for two years, and by early this year she doubted whether she could reach 70 meters. Her outlook changed after throwing 67 meters at the Diamond League final in Brussels. "Even with so little systematic training, I could get this result, so I don't think the gap to the top is big," she said. "If I can prepare well this winter, 70 meters is not out of reach." Feng is now targeting gold at next year's World Championships in Beijing and the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. "I will definitely go to the Los Angeles Olympics, and I'm going for gold," she said. "Difficulties won't knock me down. They only make me stronger." Shi Yuhao delivered China's second athletics gold of the night at Mizuho Stadium, winning the men's long jump with a season-best 8.17m on his second attempt. Hangzhou Asian Games champion Murali Sreeshankar of India took silver with 8.07m, while Uzbekistan's Anvar Anvarov finished third with 8.06m. Shi, 28, said injuries and rehabilitation had dominated much of the decade since his breakthrough at 18. "Injuries, time off and treatment took up most of the last 10 years," he said. "Even now, my foot still hurt this morning after yesterday's qualifying." The setbacks, Shi said, had taught him patience. "Early fame isn't always a good thing. Now I have to find my form again step by step," he said. China then swept the men's and women's 4x100m relay titles. Liang Xiaojing, Liu Guoyi, Liu Xiajun and Chen Yujie combined to win the women's relay in 42.96. Thailand took silver in 43.51, while Japan was just 0.01 behind in third. It was a third medal of the Games for the 17-year-old Chen, who had already won the women's 100m and taken silver in the 200m. China's Chen Jinfeng, Zeng Keli, Wang Shengjie and Xie Zhenye won the men's 4x100m relay in 38.17. Chinese Taipei took silver in 38.32 and South Korea bronze in 38.43. In other finals Monday, Japan's Ryuji Miura won the men's 3,000m steeplechase, Sri Lanka's Rumesh Tharanga claimed the men's javelin title and Kenyan-born Bahraini Winfred Yavi won the women's 5,000m. The first round of the mixed 4x100m relay was also held Monday, with China winning its heat to advance to the final. Enditem

item.title: China opens four high-speed rail lines, expanding national network
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-28
The first train of Yichang-Xingshan high-speed railway, G6888, departs from Xingshan Railway Station in Xingshan County, central China's Hubei Province, Sept. 28, 2026. The 101-kilometer Yichang-Xingshan high-speed railway officially entered service on Monday. The railway, with a designed speed of 350 kilometers per hour, is an important part of the country's high-speed rail network. (Photo by Zou Yuanjing/Xinhua) BEIJING, Sept. 28 (Xinhua) -- China, home to the world's largest high-speed rail network, opened four major high-speed railway sections to traffic on Monday, improving transport links across several regions. The new sections connect Xiong'an in Hebei Province with Shangqiu in Henan Province, Xi'an with Ankang in Shaanxi Province, Yichang with Xingshan in Hubei Province, and Harbin with Yichun in Heilongjiang Province. Spanning northern, northwestern, central and northeastern China, the new lines will facilitate travel for residents, improve regional connectivity and support economic development. In north China, the Xiong'an-Shangqiu section runs through Xiong'an New Area, Cangzhou, Hengshui and Xingtai in Hebei Province, Liaocheng in Shandong Province, Puyang in Henan Province, and Jining and Heze in Shandong Province before reaching Shangqiu in Henan Province, with the main line measuring 552 kilometers long. "Once the section begins operations, the fastest journey from Xiong'an to Shangqiu will take just 2 hours and 27 minutes," said Han Yong, deputy director of the passenger transport center of China Railway Beijing Group Co., Ltd., adding that the route will further strengthen communications between Xiong'an New Area and China's vast northern and central markets. In northwest China, the 171-km Xi'an-Ankang section crosses the Qinling Mountains, overcoming complex geological challenges while also prioritizing ecological protection. With a design speed of 350 km per hour, the train can travel between its two terminal stations in just 45 minutes. Construction of the Yichang-Xingshan section in central China faced similar challenges, with the railway traversing the Daba Mountains through a 16.9-km-long deep-buried tunnel and a high-rise mega bridge. The Yichang-Xingshan line connects China's two major high-speed railway arteries, namely the Shanghai-Chongqing-Chengdu high-speed railway along the Yangtze River and the Zhengzhou-Chongqing high-speed railway, and will unleash fresh development momentum along the Yangtze River Economic Belt, according to China Railway Wuhan Bureau Group Co., Ltd., its operator. In northeast China, the 318-km Harbin-Yichun section is China's northernmost high-speed railway ever constructed. Its terminal, Yichun West Station, is located at 47 degrees north latitude, making it China's first high-speed railway station building constructed in a permafrost region, said Shi Qinwei, head of the Yichun West Station project at China Railway Construction Group Co., Ltd. Linking Harbin, China's renowned winter destination in Heilongjiang Province with Yichun, the province's forest-enclosed haven for summer retreat, the route will cut the railway travel time between the two cities from about seven hours to roughly two hours, while extending China's modern high-speed rails to the lesser-tapped northern regions. Opened shortly before the National Day holiday, the new railways are also expected to boost tourist flows between China's major cities along the route, as well as iconic attractions such as Yichang's Three Gorges Dam and Yichun's emerald forests. China State Railway Group Co., Ltd., the country's railroad operator, is expecting some 284 million passenger trips during the Mid-Autumn Festival and National Day holiday period, which extends from Sept. 23 to October 8. China is expanding and optimizing its high-speed rail network to better serve its booming domestic markets and industries. By the end of 2025, the country's total operating railway mileage had reached 165,000 km, including more than 50,000 km of high-speed rail. Fixed-asset investment in the railway sector totaled 511.8 billion yuan (about 75.9 billion U.S. dollars) in the first eight months of the year, up 1.5 percent year on year, according to China State Railway Group Co., Ltd. Under national plans, China's high-speed rail network is projected to hit 70,000 km by 2035, with eight north-south vertical lines and eight east-west horizontal lines. Once complete, the network will connect major cities, city clusters and key economic zones throughout the country. ■ An aerial drone photo shows the high-speed train G3950 pulling out of the Heze East Railway Station in Heze City, east China's Shandong Province, Sept. 28, 2026. item.title: Out of the robot classroom: China's embodied AI takes on real-world jobs
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-28
BEIJING, Sept. 28 (Xinhua) -- Graduation day is no longer just for humans. Thirty robots made up the first class at a robot school in Hangzhou, east China's Zhejiang Province. After more than two months of training, four have graduated and landed formal jobs. One works as a museum guide in Hangzhou. Another gives tours at the robot school. A third conducts inspections at a Nestlé production workshop in Tianjin. The fourth has traveled to the Republic of Korea for piano performances. Their deployment highlights a key challenge in bringing embodied AI into the real world: training robots may require more than individual robot makers or users can provide. It demands shared infrastructure where machines can be trained, tested and improved at scale. In Xiong'an, a "city of the future" being built about 105 km southwest of Beijing, different types of robots are learning daily tasks such as taking out the trash, organizing shelves, and moving goods at a dedicated training facility. Human instructors train robots in full-scale replicas of real workplaces and public spaces. They use virtual-reality headsets and exoskeletons to operate robots as they perform tasks in simulated environments. Preparing a human for a job is no easy task, and neither is training a robot. "It took more than 1,000 repetitions just to teach the robot the basic movement of picking something up," said Liu Rui, an instructor with a digital-urban-technology subsidiary of China Xiong'an Group. Then came the full sequence: picking up a piece of trash, standing upright and putting it into a bin. Learning those three steps took another week. Every attempt also generates training data. Instructors label the data, break movements down into smaller steps and identify objects in each frame. This helps robots recognize what they see and decide how to act. By the end of June, China had completed or brought into operation more than 70 robot training facilities, with over 40 others under construction or on the drawing board, according to the China Academy of Information and Communications Technology. This expanding network is increasingly part of China's broader AI and robotics ecosystem. In 2025, more than 6,200 AI companies were operating in the country, with the core industry valued at over 1.2 trillion yuan (around 173.9 billion U.S. dollars), according to the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology. China also developed more than 400 complete humanoid robot products in 2025, accounting for more than half of the global total, according to official data. In the first half of 2026, Chinese manufacturers accounted for 97 percent of humanoid robot shipments worldwide, according to a report released at the 2026 World Robot Conference. Jiang Lei, chief scientist at the National and Local Co-Built Humanoid Robotics Innovation Center, said embodied AI robots had moved from "zero to one," but scaling from "one to 10" remained a challenge. The bottlenecks, he said, lie in standards, engineering management and pilot-scale testing. At the heart of it all is the ability to adapt robots to different real-world scenarios. China's vast manufacturing base gives robot makers not only a large market, but also a wide range of real-world and simulated environments in which to train, test and refine their machines. A DATA MEGAFACTORY The rise of robot schools and training bases is turning training data into an economic resource -- a critical input for bringing embodied AI into the real world. Large language models and multimodal AI systems have advanced rapidly by drawing on accumulated written material and vast amounts of internet data. Embodied AI, by contrast, must learn to act in the physical world, which requires data generated through real-world interactions. A factory, warehouse or restaurant may demand different levels of force, precision and movement. With so many scenarios to cover, getting enough high-quality training data remains costly and challenging. Much of that data has never been systematically collected, processed or stored, industry analysts say. When China Xiong'an Group worked to integrate its digital platform more closely with the physical city in 2025, leading AI model companies approached the group to purchase high-quality datasets totaling tens of millions of hours. At the robot school in Xiong'an, training datasets are used to train AI models and fed into an urban data space, where they can later be shared and traded, said Cao Yue, a manager at the group's digital-urban-technology subsidiary. In that sense, the robot school is also a "megafactory" producing the data fuel for embodied AI training. At a national pilot base for embodied AI applications in Hangzhou, companies can access computing power, data, model services and scenario testing through a public technical platform. "Companies once spent tens of millions of yuan on training data alone to develop a single real-world application. Now, by joining the base, startups can tap national-level innovation resources in one place, significantly reducing R&D costs at the pilot stage," said Zhang Haiwei, founder of a robotics technology company in Hangzhou. The idea is straightforward: instead of every company building its own training ground, data pipeline and testing environment, shared facilities can spread the cost and make it easier to turn laboratory prototypes into machines that can actually work. THE HUMAN QUESTION As more robots move into the workplace -- some after training at dedicated robot schools -- another question is coming to the fore: What happens to human workers? Yu Jiang, a researcher at the Chinese Academy of Sciences, said technological revolutions may eliminate some jobs, but also create new ones. "When cars replaced horse-drawn carriages, for example, some coachmen became drivers," he said. Xiong Rong, a professor at Zhejiang University, said robots would increasingly take over repetitive, strenuous and high-risk work, while people focus on management, technology and innovation. Earlier this month, China added 11 occupations to its list of officially recognized professions, including embodied AI robot application technicians and AI agent developers. Experts noted that lifelong learning and vocational reskilling are essential for workers to adapt to a new work ecosystem that combines human judgment, empathy and creativity with robotic precision and endurance. ■

item.title: Xi stresses advancing Peaceful China Initiative to safeguard Chinese modernization
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-28
BEIJING, Sept. 28 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping has urged efforts to advance the Peaceful China Initiative to a higher level to ensure steady and sustained progress in Chinese modernization. Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks in his recent instruction on the initiative. In his instruction, Xi stated that since the 18th CPC National Congress in 2012, significant progress has been made in building a safe China, making the country one of the safest in the world. He emphasized efforts to resolutely pursue a holistic approach to national security and to uphold and strengthen the Party's overall leadership in this area. He also called for efforts to both pursue development and safeguard security, strengthen the legal underpinning, leverage science and technology, and prevent and mitigate all kinds of risks in relevant fields, so as to continuously make the country safer, society more orderly, governance more effective, and the people more satisfied. Xi's instruction was conveyed at a working conference on the initiative held Monday in Beijing. Chen Wenqing, a member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and head of the Commission for Political and Legal Affairs of the CPC Central Committee, attended the conference and gave a speech. He noted that the Peaceful China Initiative has produced results that have won worldwide recognition and safety has become a distinctive hallmark of China's governance. Chen called for an approach that combines punishment and prevention to create synergy and urged greater efforts to advance the Peaceful China Initiative to a higher level. Wang Xiaohong, a member of the Secretariat of the CPC Central Committee and minister of public security, pledged that the implementation will focus on key tasks, innovative methods and strengthened foundations at primary levels. China is among the countries with the lowest rates of crime and homicide. A recently released Global Public Security Index Report (2025-2026) showed that the country topped the index with a score of 84.62 points. The findings echo the international perception of China's strong public safety record. More international travelers are experiencing that sense of security firsthand as visa-free access expands, travel services improve and urban support systems are strengthened. At Monday's conference, 60 cities and 160 counties were designated as models for advancing the Peaceful China Initiative and awarded honoring plaques. ■
